technical_and_design_decisions: Implement batching for Rabbit sink using Spring Integration's batching support and RabbitMQ properties for efficient data writing.
Configure Gradle build with module layout to declare Spring XD dependencies as provided, based on Spring Boot's module layout scoping.
Write acceptance tests for hdfs-dataset using Spring Test framework with mocking or test HDFS environment for CI integration.
Extend compression support by allowing custom Compressor implementations in the configuration for user overrides.
Make database requirement optional by introducing conditional configuration, enabling DIRT runtime for stream processing only.
Implement RxJava processor interface using Spring's Reactive Streams support to facilitate processor module creation.
assumptions: The development environment is set up with Java 17+, Spring Framework 6.0+, Gradle, and all necessary tools and libraries.
Existing codebase follows standard Spring patterns, allowing reuse of similar structures for new features.
Performance benchmarks will leverage existing infrastructure, metrics collection tools, and previous baseline snapshots.
No major external dependencies are required; all features can be implemented using standard Spring and third-party components already in use.
CI/CD pipeline is configured to run tests, build configurations, and performance benchmarks automatically.
Time estimates are based on a single developer with familiarity with Spring Framework and the existing project.

activities.activity_description: Understand all user stories (U1-U8), plan implementation steps, identify dependencies, and define technical approaches.
Implement code changes to support batching in Rabbit sink, including configuration options for batchingEnabled and batchingSize, and write unit tests.
Set up Gradle build script to declare Spring XD dependencies as provided, configure boot plugin for MODULE layout, and handle boilerplate configuration.
Develop acceptance tests to validate hdfs-dataset module functionality, including setup for CI builds and integration with existing test suites.
Extend compression support to allow user overrides and customization of defaults, with implementation and documentation.
Setup and configure benchmarks for Rabbit sink with batching and compression options, and rerun baseline performance tests for comparison.
Implement option to disable database requirement, making it optional for DIRT runtime, with configuration changes and tests.
Implement core interface contract for creating processor modules using RxJava API, including interface definition and sample implementation.
Perform end-to-end integration testing to ensure all new features work together correctly and do not break existing functionality.
Review code for quality, adhere to best practices, refactor as needed, and ensure consistency across all changes.
Update or create documentation for new features, configuration options, and any architectural changes made during development.
